finding: Material hierarchy is legible by category but not by world priority: the 13 working agent spheres use a bright cyan fill with near-white stroke, while the WORLD root uses a dark fill with a bright cyan stroke and an additional cyan torus. In the rendered artifact, the repeated floor tiles and the luminous agent nodes compete with the root; the root reads as another node instead of the primary substrate/anchor.

candidate_change.change: Assign the WORLD root a distinct, higher-value substrate material: raise its fill from #152B31 to a restrained warm light material and keep the ring as a lower-contrast edge, while lowering working-node stroke brightness from #E8FFFF to the working fill family (#70E5F2). Keep idle nodes gray and task parcels gold unchanged.
candidate_change.intended_result: The eye should read WORLD first, working traces second, task parcels third, and the habitat floor last, without changing geometry, copy, source data, or status semantics.

evidence.observation: The habitat floor is built from 35 repeated tiles with fill #101B21 and stroke #24363C; this creates a large, repeated material field behind all entities.
The WORLD root has dark fill #152B31, bright #A3E9F0 stroke, and a separate #58C9D8 torus; its material family overlaps the working traces.
Working and idle nodes are differentiated by fill/color, but working nodes also receive near-white #E8FFFF strokes and are rendered as bright spheres.
Sampled frames show the cyan/white agent spheres and root ring competing for the strongest cool highlight; the floor tile grid remains visually persistent.
The source is a read-only snapshot with 13 working agents, 2 idle agents, 60 tasks, and fake_evidence=false; the candidate does not alter these source facts.

falsifier: After the candidate render, if blinded viewers still identify a working agent or task parcel as the primary anchor before WORLD in at least 4 of 5 trials, or if the root becomes less distinguishable from the floor, this material-only hypothesis is falsified.
next_measurement: Render the unchanged shot and the candidate at the same 854x480 settings. Use the final six sampled frames and a 5-person blinded identification test. Record first-identified anchor (WORLD / working node / task parcel / floor), plus mean luminance and edge contrast for masked WORLD, working-node, task-parcel, and floor regions. Accept only if WORLD is first in at least 4/5 trials, working-vs-idle remains distinguishable, and no source/copy/geometry diff is introduced.
